def count_winning_first_moves(lamps):
    """
    Rectangle-corner lamp game.

    The board is the 24x24 grid of cells (r, c) with 0 <= r, c <= 23.
    `lamps` is a list of distinct (r, c) integer tuples: the cells whose
    lamp is initially ON (0 <= len(lamps) <= 576). All other lamps are OFF.

    Two players alternate moves. A move chooses four cells that form the
    corners of an axis-aligned rectangle with positive width and height:
    (r1, c1), (r1, c2), (r2, c1), (r2, c2) with 0 <= r1 < r2 <= 23 and
    0 <= c1 < c2 <= 23, subject to one legality condition: the lamp at
    (r2, c2) (the corner with maximal row AND maximal column) must
    currently be ON. The move toggles all four corner lamps (ON becomes
    OFF, OFF becomes ON). A player who has no legal move loses.

    (Every move switches the lamp at (r2, c2) OFF and otherwise toggles
    only cells that are earlier in row-major order, so the lamp pattern
    read in row-major order as a binary number strictly decreases; hence
    the game is finite.)

    Return the number of distinct legal first moves (moves are identified
    by the quadruple (r1, c1, r2, c2)) after which the mover can force a
    win under optimal play by both sides, i.e. moves leading to a position
    that is a loss for the player then to move. If the starting position
    is a loss for the first player (in particular, if there is no legal
    move at all), return 0.

    Note: brute-force game search is hopeless: there are up to 2^576
    reachable lamp patterns.

    >>> count_winning_first_moves([(1, 1)])
    1
    >>> count_winning_first_moves([(1, 2), (2, 1)])
    0
    >>> count_winning_first_moves([(1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2)])
    3
    """
